title: Time
intro: This unit contains the book's worst traps for an English speaker: tiempo, vez, mañana and tarde each carry two meanings that English splits into different words.

entries.note: Uncountable time, and the weather. For a countable occasion use vez.

ex.en: I don't have time this week.
What's the weather like in Bogotá?

entries.note: Countable times. Plural veces. A veces = sometimes, otra vez = again, tal vez = maybe.

ex.en: I told you three times.
Maybe he'll come later.

entries.note: The tilde matters: ano without it is a part of the body.

ex.es: El año pasado viajamos a Perú.
ex.en: Last year we travelled to Peru.

entries.note: Ends in -a but is masculine: el día, un buen día. Words from Greek often behave this way.

ex.es: Trabajo todos los días menos el domingo.
ex.en: I work every day except Sunday.

ex.es: Nos vemos la semana que viene.
ex.en: We'll see each other next week.

ex.es: Pago la renta a fin de mes.
ex.en: I pay the rent at the end of the month.
We waited half an hour.
What time does the train leave?

ex.es: En ese momento sonó el teléfono.
ex.en: At that moment the phone rang.

ex.es: No es el momento de hablar de eso.
ex.en: This isn't the time to talk about that.

entries.note: With the article it is the morning; bare, it is tomorrow. Both at once: mañana por la mañana.

ex.en: I run every morning.

ex.es: Mañana tengo una cita con el médico.
ex.en: Tomorrow I have a doctor's appointment.
I'm leaving tomorrow morning.

entries.note: La tarde stretches until dark, so it covers both English afternoon and evening.

ex.en: We'll see each other in the afternoon.
He went to bed very late.
He arrived late in the afternoon.
Last night I slept badly.
I'm not working today.
It was very windy yesterday.

entries.note: ahora mismo = right now. por ahora = for the time being.

ex.en: I'm busy right now.

entries.note: Hasta luego is the everyday goodbye.

ex.en: I'll call you later.
First we eat and then we go out.
He always forgets his keys.

entries.note: After the verb it needs a no in front of it: no voy nunca. Before the verb it stands alone: nunca voy.

ex.en: I've never been to Mexico.
I get up early on weekdays.

entries.note: Interchangeable with aún in most sentences.

ex.en: He still lives with his parents.
It isn't ready yet.
He reads the paper while he has breakfast.
